methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops delivered by a Norfolk native signal grassroots knowledge distribution outside metro hubs, building peer-to-peer fluency that could counteract NoVA concentration if sustained and scaled across underserved regions.

signals.title: Virginia Tech sets course for human-centered AI leadership - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's institutional AI leadership initiative deepens technical capability in Blacksburg but signals concentration in established research centers rather than broad workforce distribution across Southwest and Southside regions.

signals.title: Camp Welcomes Hampton Roads Youth to Learn About Cybersecurity and AI - Old Dominion University
signals.signal_reading: Youth-focused cybersecurity and AI camps at ODU indicate early-stage capability building in Hampton Roads' defense-adjacent ecosystem, creating distributed foundational fluency that could mature into deep expertise if pathways persist beyond one-time events.

signals.title: UVA study explores the role of Artificial Intelligence in special education - WVIR
signals.signal_reading: UVA research exploring AI in special education demonstrates deep capability concentration in flagship universities, but application in K-12 settings could distribute shallow adoption statewide if implementation reaches rural school systems beyond the research phase.

signals.title: Roanoke College joins Google AI for Education Accelerator - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's Google AI partnership signals platform-mediated adoption in smaller institutions, enabling distributed but potentially shallow implementation where faculty use pre-built tools rather than developing indigenous AI expertise.
